transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I’m not wasting your time with this. I really don't want to be a bother, but... well, for over a year now, I’ve been trying to get someone to just take me seriously about some things happening at work. 

I'm in computer support, and... well, they started this new ticket rotation and these extra security audits. I know it probably sounds silly to bring up, and I really don't want to come across as a difficult employee, but it just seems like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. 

I've tried to be professional about it, but management keeps pulling up the system logs and telling me it’s just standard policy. I want to believe them, I really do, because I've always prided myself on being a good team player. Does that make sense? I just... I want to make sure I'm handling this appropriately and not making a fuss over nothing.
Have you noticed yourself feeling this same sense of suspicion or distrust toward people in other areas of your life, such as with your friends or family?

Oh, no, no. Please don't think that. I... I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm just suspicious of everyone around me. It's really only this one specific situation at the office. 

Outside of that whole issue with the ticket rotation and the audits, everything is perfectly fine. I still keep the house in order, make sure all the bills are paid on time, and... well, I try my best to be a good husband and help my wife out however I can. And even at work, I'm still handling all the technical parts of my job just fine. Nobody has ever complained that my work is sloppy or disorganized. I've always been very diligent about my actual duties. 

I hope that makes sense? I just... I really want you to know that I'm still keeping everything else together, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just looking for problems where there aren't any.
Outside of this situation at work, do you find yourself feeling constantly worried or anxious about other aspects of your daily life, such as your health, finances, or your family's safety?

Oh, goodness, no. No, not at all. I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I'm... well, that I'm just an anxious person in general. I really don't want you to think I'm a nervous wreck or anything like that. 

My health is pretty good for a guy my age, thank goodness, and, um, I've always been very careful with our savings, so our finances are perfectly fine. My wife and I are very secure there. It's really... it's honestly just this one situation at the office that's been weighing on me so heavily. Everything else in my life is completely normal and steady, I promise. 

Is it okay that I'm just focusing on the work thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and not making myself sound like the sort of person who just worries about every little thing, because I'm really not.
Have you spoken to any coworkers or friends about these audits, and if so, do they agree that management is targeting you?

Well, I... I haven't really talked to anyone else about it, to be honest. I didn't want to drag anyone else into it, or, you know, seem like I was gossiping or complaining behind management's back. I've always tried to be very professional and keep my head down. 

I did sort of mention the new ticket rotation to one of the other guys on the team once, just in passing, but... well, he just said it was probably some new corporate policy and shrugged it off. I didn't push it, because I really don't want to be seen as a troublemaker or someone who stirs up drama in the office. 

I hope that was the right way to handle it? I just thought it was best to keep it to myself and try to deal with it on my own, rather than making a big fuss and bothering my coworkers. I really do try to be a good employee, I promise.

When your manager or coworkers explain that these audits are just standard company policy, do you feel that they are actually telling you the truth, or do you remain convinced that they are intentionally misleading you to cover up their true intentions?

Well, I... I know they say it's standard policy. And they've even sat me down and showed me the logs, pointing out how it's supposedly random or just part of the new system. And I really do try to listen, I do. I don't want you to think I'm just being stubborn or ignoring them. 

But... well, I've been trying to get someone to take this seriously for over a year now. Because even when they show me those logs, I just... I can't shake the feeling that it's all being used to build a paper trail against me. Like it's a way to quietly push me out. 

I hope I don't sound unreasonable saying that. I know how it must sound to someone on the outside, and I really don't want to come across as difficult or paranoid. It's just... when you're the one going through it for that long, it's hard to just accept that it's normal policy, you know? Does that make sense? I'm really trying to be objective about it, I promise.
Aside from your concerns about the situation at work, have you ever heard voices or noticed any other sensations that others around you do not seem to experience?

Oh, no. No, nothing like that at all. I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there, or anything of that sort. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm... well, that I'm losing touch with reality or something. 

My mind is perfectly clear, I assure you. I'm just a regular guy trying to do his job, and I've never had any sort of hallucinations or anything like that. I know that's a very serious thing, and I wouldn't want you to think I'm dealing with that kind of issue. 

Is it okay that I'm being so firm about that? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly and that you know I'm completely grounded, aside from this one very specific situation at the office. I'm really trying to give you the most accurate picture I can.
Do you ever feel as though your thoughts or actions are being controlled by outside forces or people at your office, rather than by your own free will?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I make all my own choices. My thoughts are entirely my own. I mean, management might control the servers and the ticket queues at work, but they certainly don't control my mind or my actions. 

I really hope I haven't said anything to make you think I believe something like that. I know how bizarre that would sound, like something out of a science fiction movie. I'm completely in control of myself, I promise. I'm just a normal guy trying to navigate a really unfair situation at the office, but I know where the boundary is between their actions and my own mind. 

Is that... did I answer that okay? I just want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to understand where I'm coming from. I really want to be as helpful and cooperative as possible.
Do you believe that the people at your work are acting alone, or do you suspect that they might be coordinating with others outside of the company to monitor or target you?

Oh, no, definitely not. I don't think there's some... grand conspiracy outside the company or anything like that. It's just the people in my department, the ones who handle the logs and the assignments. 

I know sometimes people get carried away and think the whole world is against them, but I'm really not like that. I'm very realistic about it. It's just a localized issue with management and a few coworkers trying to push an older guy out, you know? Nothing involving the government or outside agencies or anything crazy. 

I hope that shows I'm keeping things in perspective. I really try to be level-headed about all this. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you reasonable answers.
Are there any other beliefs or convictions you hold that other people, perhaps even your wife, have told you seem unlikely or untrue?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, my wife and I might disagree on little things, like... oh, I don't know, whether I spend too much time worrying about the office, but she doesn't think I believe anything untrue. 

I really try to keep myself grounded, you know? I don't have any strange ideas or... or weird theories about how the world works. I'm just a regular guy who goes to work, comes home, and tries to do the right thing. I wouldn't want you to think I'm walking around with a head full of wild ideas. 

I'm pretty normal in that regard, I think. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I really don't want to come across as someone who is... well, difficult or out of touch.
How much of your time each day do you find yourself thinking about these audits and this situation at work?

Oh, well, I wouldn't say it takes up too much of my day. I mean, naturally, when I'm at the office, I have to be aware of what's happening with the assignments and the logs. But once I clock out, I really try to leave it at the door. 

I might think about it for a few minutes on the drive home, just trying to make sure I didn't miss anything that they could use against me, but I definitely don't let it consume my life. I still enjoy my evenings, you know? I watch TV, spend time with my wife. I'm not sitting up all night obsessing over it. 

I hope that sounds like a healthy balance? I really try my best not to let it take over, because I know that wouldn't be good for me. I just want to make sure I'm handling it the right way... does that seem like a normal amount of time to you?
